Wow, you've gotten impressively far for 2 weeks!

You shouldn't need the jQuery at all. Instead, when you call updateSelectedInput, pass a named vector for choices; the name will be used as the label, and the value will be used as the value. In this case, if it's the index that you want, then you can use something like:

choices <- 1:nrow(business_list())
names(choices) <- business_list()$name
updateSelectInput(session, "search_result", choices = c(
  if (business_list()$name[1] != "No result") c("Please select a restaurant"=""),
  choices
))

Then the value in input$search_result will be a row number (as a string, unfortunately for this case) instead of a name.

You might also create a reactive like this:

selected_business <- reactive({
  if (input$search_result == "")
    return(NULL)
  return(business_list()[as.numeric(input$search_result),])
})

Then everywhere else you can simply do selected_business()$image_b, etc.

source("Analytics API.R")

  business_list <- reactive({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    withProgress(session, min=0, max=10, {
      setProgress(message="Searching",
                  detail="This may take a while...")
      isolate({
        result <- search_business(input$businessName, input$businessLocation)
      })
      for (i in 1:50) {
        setProgress(value = i)
      }
      return(result)
    })
    
  })

    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
    if (input$selIdx == 0) return()
    withProgress(session, min=0, max=10, {
      setProgress(message="Downloading reviews",
                  detail="This may take a while...")

        setProgress(value = i)
      }
      return(data)
    })
  })
  
  observe({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "search_result",
                      "",
                      c(if(business_list()$name[1] != "No result") "Please select a restaurant",

                      selected=NULL)

   if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
   data <- get_business_data()
   data

               bAutoWidth=FALSE,
               aoColumns=NULL,
               aoColumnDefs = list(list(sWidth="7em",
                                        aTargets=c(list(0),list(1))))))
  
  output$business_info <- renderUI({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
    if (input$selIdx == 0) return()
    name <- paste("<b>Name: </b>", as.character(business_list()$name[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    rating <- paste("<b>Rating: </b>", as.character(business_list()$rating[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    address <- paste("<b>Address: </b>", as.character(business_list()$address[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    url <- paste("<b>Yelp URL: </b>", as.character(business_list()$url_b[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    HTML(paste(name, rating, address, url, sep="<br/>"))
  })
  
  output$business_image <- renderUI({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
    if (input$selIdx == 0) return()
    image_b <- paste("<br/><img src='",
                     as.character(business_list()$image_b[input$selIdx]),
                     "' alt='business-image' height='150' width='150'>",
                     sep="")
    HTML(image_b)
  })

  
})

2. If the user clicks the "Search" action button, then call Yelp API (search API) to retrieve business list
3. With that list, updateSelectInput
4. If index of SelectInput changes, then show business_info & business_image & table

$(document).ready(function(){

Shiny.onInputChange('selIdx', this.selectedIndex);

})

input$searchAction == 0 means that button has NEVER been clicked.

I don't think you should have renderDataTable refer to searchAction directly. Rather, have it use the selected_business() reactive, and if it's NULL, just return nothing from renderDataTable.

As for the comma when using [ ] with a data frame, that's the syntax for extracting entire rows from a data frame. See this link:
http://www.r-tutor.com/r-introduction/data-frame/data-frame-row-slice

The NA might be because there are "" values in there or something. You'll have to look and see what the values are; try inserting a browser() call around there, that'll drop you into a shell where you can inspect the values directly. (Or if you're using RStudio, then browser() will activate the debugger)
